teaches: When you are attacking, sort your pawns by what they are doing rather than by whether they can be taken. A pawn that shuts an enemy piece out of the game is part of the attack and must not be traded away to save something else; a pawn on the far side of the board that no piece is using can simply be allowed to fall.
explains: The queen has to choose a square, and the pawn on b2 is hanging. It can be left: the knight that takes it is out of play, and the attack continues with the knight coming to g5 regardless. What matters far more is the pawn on e5, which is the reason the bishop on g7 has nothing to look at — the queen belongs where it keeps that pawn and the attacking pieces together.
